To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the immunotoxicity observed in rats perinatally exposed to Baltic Sea hering oil or 2.3,7, 8-tetrachloredibenzo-p-diooxin (TCDD), was characterized by reduced thymi and splenic cellularity, reduced proliferative responses of splenocytes in vitro, and impaired natural killer (NK)-cell function.
exposure to complex mixtures of PHAHs in the Baltic Sea herry oil, which are known to be immunotoxic, resulted in a transient immunosuppression in the rat pups.

exposure of pregnant rats to Baltic Sea herryng oil or 2.3,7, 8-TCDD during pregnancy and lactaton resulted in immunosupression and impaired resistance to RCMV infection in the offspring, and that these effects were transient, possibly due to the rapid elimination of TCDD.

the immunotoxic potential and mechanisms of action of environmental mixtures of PHAHs in mammals.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Baltic Sea hering oil extract is not immunotoxic in rats, but the 2, 3, 7, 8-TCDD-spiked herring oil extract is immunotoxic in rats.

the immunotoxicity observed in rats exposed perinally to Baltic herring oil or TCDD was not a result of the Ah-receptor agonistic activity of the oil or TCDD, but of the immunotoxicity associated with other constituents of the oil.
the immune response of the offspring is affected by the perinatal exposure of the pregnant female to a mixture of PHAHs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Baltic herring oil is a complex mixture of PHAHs which are immunotoxic to rats and seals at current levels in Baltic herring, and that the developing immune function of young rats and seals is more susceptible to the toxic effects of these PHAHs.
the Baltic Sea hering oil is not as immunotoxic as TCDD, but it is still immunotoxic.
exposure to the Baltic Sea Herring Oil or 2, 3, 7, 8-TCDD during pregnancy and lactations leads to impaired cellular immune response in rat offspring.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the developing immune systems of young mammals, including humans, are at particular risk to the effects of environmental contaminants.
the developing immune function of young mammals, including humans, may be at particular immunotoxicological risk from complex mixtures of dioxin-like compounds in the aquatic environment.
exposure of developing mammals to complex mixtures of PHAHs can result in immunotoxic effects.
